plan.hypothesis: An external IP brute-forced SSH on DEMO-SSH and then logged in successfully on 2026-10-25.

steps.purpose: Sources with many failed SSH logins
Brute-force candidates (sources with many failed SSH logins); successful logins after them are searched by the Hunter

success_criteria: T1110 (Brute Force): at least 1 independent self-checked indicator(s)
T1078 (Valid Accounts): at least 1 independent self-checked indicator(s)
refutation_criteria: T1110: all required sources and fields covered for the full window AND zero indicators
T1078: all required sources and fields covered for the full window AND zero indicators

claims.text: Source 203.0.113.99 logged in successfully as demo on DEMO-SSH after its failed SSH logins began (30 failures from this source in the window)

dynamic_steps.purpose: Successful SSH logins from 203.0.113.99 after its first failed login (2026-10-25T00:10:00.000Z)
dynamic_steps.claim_template: Source {source.ip} logged in successfully as {user.name} on {host.name} after its failed SSH logins began ({failed_logins} failures from this source in the window)

limitations: Findings depend on the playbooks used; techniques without a playbook are not tested.
Baselines are synthetic allowlists and must be tuned per environment.
NOT_SUPPORTED means no evidence within the covered sources, fields and window, not proof of absence.
Claims passed C2's structural self-check only; independent re-verification against Elasticsearch is C3's.

c2_verdict.label: SUPPORTED
reasons: Every required technique has at least the minimum number of independent self-checked indicators.
review_reasons: SUPPORTED verdicts always require analyst review
